title: Study session report
goal: Build a plain JavaScript module that validates study-session data, summarizes progress, formats a report, and loads optional remote sessions.
requirements: Keep sessions as an array of objects
Use pure functions for filtering and totals
Return useful empty and error states
Export the report functions as a module

steps.title: Model one session
steps.task: Create an object with topic, minutes, score, and completed.
steps.code: const session = { topic: "Arrays", minutes: 25, score: 80, completed: true };
steps.check: Every property has the intended type.
steps.reason: Clear values and object shape make later logic predictable.

steps.title: Validate the boundary
steps.task: Reject missing topic and invalid minutes.
steps.code: function isValidSession({ topic, minutes }) { return typeof topic === "string" && topic.trim() && Number.isFinite(minutes) && minutes >= 0; }
steps.check: Invalid or negative minutes return false.
steps.reason: Boundary validation prevents bad data from spreading.

steps.title: Select completed work
steps.task: Use filter without changing the input array.
steps.check: The result contains only completed sessions and the input is unchanged.
steps.reason: filter expresses selection and returns a new array.

steps.title: Calculate totals
steps.code: const totalMinutes = sessions => sessions.reduce((total, session) => total + session.minutes, 0);
steps.reason: The explicit initial value makes the empty case safe.

steps.title: Build an immutable summary
steps.code: const summarize = sessions => ({ count: sessions.length, minutes: totalMinutes(sessions), topics: sessions.map(({ topic }) => topic) });
steps.check: The function does not write to sessions.
steps.reason: A new result keeps data flow visible.

steps.title: Format missing values
steps.task: Use optional chaining and a nullish fallback.
steps.check: An empty string remains an empty string; null becomes Learner.
steps.reason: Nullish fallback preserves valid falsy values.

steps.title: Load remote data safely
steps.task: Fetch JSON and reject non-success status.
steps.code: async function loadSessions(url) { const response = await fetch(url); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`); return response.json(); }
steps.check: 404 becomes a handled error rather than false success.
steps.reason: fetch needs an explicit HTTP status check.

steps.title: Test timing and errors
steps.task: Call the report from a timer and catch failures.
steps.check: Explain why the callback runs after current synchronous code.
steps.reason: The final step connects promises, timers, and error flow.

acceptanceScenarios.then: All numeric totals are zero and topics is empty
Only valid sessions contribute to the report
The returned promise rejects with the HTTP status

extensions: Group minutes by topic with reduce.
Render the summary in a small React component after rebuilding it independently.
